why_this_exists: the experiment acquired three surfaces it was not pre-registered on, and until this file there was no rule for weighing four readings. Choosing that rule after seeing arm A's numbers is how a one-knob A/B becomes a survey with a preferred answer. Raised by the parallel audit session as one of four checks it intends to run on the finished verdict; this closes it in advance rather than defending it afterwards.
written_before: any arm A reading existed. Verifiable: at the time of writing there is no starlight_l1arm.json under datasets/aug06/l1_work/ and none under any set's starlight_work/, and the 13 arm A members are still building. Every number the rule depends on comes from the CONTROL surfaces and arm B, all of which were measured earlier and are on disk.
rule_1_the_primary_surface_is_the_union: the pre-registration names ONE surface, the 3-set union, and its reading IS the pre-registered result. falsifier_arm_A and falsifier_arm_B are evaluated there, by name, against the pre-registered 0.90 line. Whatever the union gives is what the experiment answers — including CONFIRMED-AS-EQUIVALENT, and including a null. No per-set reading can change that verdict.
rule_2_the_per_set_readings_are_a_supple: they were added AFTER the union was seen to be unable to exercise its own falsifiers, so treating them as the answer whenever they are sharper would be choosing the surface by its result. They are reported as a POWERED SUPPLEMENT: they can say what the pre-registered surface could not resolve, and they cannot overturn what it did resolve. If union and supplement disagree, the union's verdict stands as THE result and the disagreement is reported as the finding it is.
rule_3_power_is_assigned_by_a_criterion_: a surface is POWERED if, on its CONTROL, the shift-null rejects at p <= 0.05 in at least 2 of 3 channels AND the paired retained_se is <= 0.10 in all 3. Both quantities are properties of the control and arm B alone — no arm A input — so this cannot be tuned to an outcome. Applied to the four surfaces on today's numbers: set-01 POWERED (p 0.000/0.014/0.014, se 0.0558/0.0708/0.0598); set-02 POWERED (p 0.007/0.014/0.000, se 0.0723/0.0680/0.0637); set-03 NOT POWERED (p 0.381/0.403/0.151, se 0.3337/0.2974/0.1405); union NOT POWERED (p 0.266/0.252/0.230, se 0.2871/0.3162/0.1745). The union is therefore both the PRIMARY surface and an UNDER-POWERED one, and the verdict must say so in the same breath rather than choosing whichever half suits it.
rule_4_combining_the_supplement_STANDARD: AMENDED at 22:47, still with 0 of 13 arm A members built and 0 arm A records on disk — the amendment predates the data it governs exactly as the original did. The first draft said flatly 'no pooling'. That was an internal doctrine invented in place of an industry default, which CLAUDE.md's standards-first rule forbids: combining independent estimates of one quantity is META-ANALYSIS, and the field standard is a heterogeneity test followed by inverse-variance weighting (Cochran's Q; DerSimonian-Laird for the random-effects case). Adopted, with the gate doing the work my flat refusal was trying to do: (a) HETEROGENEITY GATE FIRST — if the two powered readings differ by more than 2x their combined SE, do NOT combine, because the common-quantity assumption that combining rests on is then falsified by the data; report them separately and say so. (b) IF HOMOGENEOUS — inverse-variance weighted mean with combined SE = 1/sqrt(sum(1/se^2)), computed ACROSS SETS WITHIN A CHANNEL and NEVER across channels, because the falsifier's quantifier is 'in any channel' and pooling channels would dilute exactly the thing it quantifies over. (c) the combined number is DESCRIPTIVE — it never carries a falsifier verdict of its own (rule 4b). The measured constraint that made me want to refuse is real and is now stated rather than acted on unilaterally: the surfaces have different catalogue bounds (10.0% / 7.5%), so what they estimate is only one quantity if arm A's effect is field-independent — which is precisely what the heterogeneity gate tests rather than assumes.
rule_4a_the_gate_is_WEAK_AT_n_EQUALS_2_a: the heterogeneity gate is now doing real work, so its limit is recorded rather than left for a reader to discover. A Q-style test on TWO estimates is badly under-powered: it asks whether the ESTIMATES are distinguishable given their SEs, not whether the underlying quantities are equal, and at n=2 it passes in most cases where they genuinely differ. There is also a specific reason here to expect they might: the two powered surfaces carry different catalogue plane bounds, 10.0% against 7.5%, which IS the statement that a plane reaches different fractions of the predictor's variance in the two fields. So a PASS is weak evidence of poolability and NOT a finding of homogeneity, and the record prints the gate's own numbers rather than just its verdict. Adopting the standard and recording where it is strained is what standards-first asks; adopting it silently would not be.
rule_4b_the_supplement_carries_NO_falsif: the first reason is rule 2 — a surface added after the primary one failed cannot promote itself. The second is MULTIPLICITY, and it is independent of the first. The falsifier reads 'below 0.90 IN ANY CHANNEL' and was written when there was ONE surface: three chances to fire. Evaluated on four surfaces it becomes twelve, and 'any of twelve fires' is a materially LOOSER test than the one pre-registered — looser in the direction of finding an effect, which is the direction that flatters the hypothesis. Keeping exactly ONE falsifier evaluation, on the union, preserves the operating characteristics the test was written with. The powered surfaces are therefore reported with their retained values, SEs and the distance to 0.90 in SE units, and NOT with a REFUTED/CONFIRMED verdict of their own.
rule_5_the_directional_prediction_is_tes: retained_A < retained_B is evaluated on each surface separately, against that surface's own combined SE (sqrt(SE_A^2 + SE_B^2), using arm A's MEASURED SE rather than the SE_A = SE_B projection used while arm A was building). CONFIRMED-AS-EQUIVALENT fires per surface. Every equivalence statement carries the bound from equivalence_bound_note.json — the window is the size of the whole effect an on-stack plane can have — and is never written as a bare 'equivalent'.
rule_6_what_would_make_this_rule_wrong: if arm A turns out to be measurable on the union after all — i.e. the union's retained_A lands outside the equivalence window and clear of 0.90 — then the union answers its own question and the supplement is a corroboration rather than a rescue. The rule handles that without amendment: rule 1 already gives the union the verdict. The rule only does work in the case it was written for, where the union returns an under-powered null.
rule_7_an_UNDER_POWERED_equivalence_is_r: pre-committed PHRASING, and it changes no precedence: rule 1 still gives the union the verdict and rule 2 still forbids the supplement promoting itself. But 'CONFIRMED-AS-EQUIVALENT' on a surface whose equivalence window is 6.30x / 6.93x / 3.83x the entire effect that could exist there (union bound 0.0645 against windows 0.406 / 0.447 / 0.247) asserts something the data cannot support. Equal within a window four to seven times larger than the whole measurable effect is NON-RESOLUTION, not equivalence — the same distinction already forced on arm B's component versus its reading. So: if the union returns equivalence AND the union is UNDER-POWERED by rule 3, the verdict word is NON-RESOLVED, the window/bound ratio is printed beside it, and the supplement's readings are reported in the same paragraph rather than beneath a word the union never earned. This costs the pre-registration nothing and stops the discipline manufacturing a false null.
what_this_rule_does_not_do: it does not decide the LEVEL question. The instrument gates nothing; the owner's eyes on the full-frame 16-bit PNG triple decide anything aesthetic, and if both arms preserve the starlight equally the level choice falls to the other criterion and the owner, exactly as the pre-registration says.
